svg.title: Culturing microorganisms
svg.desc: Binary fission: One bacterium divides into two. Division may take 20 minutes with enough nutrients and suitable temperature. Use the given time. 1 → 2 → 4 → 8: repeated doubling, not addition. Bacteria have no nucleus and do not use mitosis. Growing a culture: Nutrient broth: nutrients for growth. Agar: a surface for colonies, visible groups from an initial cell or group. Uncontaminated cultures allow fair comparisons. Aseptic technique: keeps unwanted microbes out. Sterile equipment: Sterilise dishes and growth medium to remove unwanted microbes. Flame the loop, then let it cool so it does not kill the culture. Open the lid briefly to limit airborne contamination. Follow school handling and disposal procedures. Safe incubation: Tape the edges: stops accidental opening. Do not seal completely. Allow gas exchange. Store upside down: stops condensation dripping onto the culture. Maximum 25°C in school: limits harmful human pathogens. Do not open incubated plates. Antimicrobial discs: Use aseptic technique to prepare a bacterial lawn on sterile agar. Add antibiotic or antiseptic discs and a solvent-only control. Incubate safely. Measure inhibition zones. Repeat and calculate a mean for each treatment. Variables & conclusions: Change: substance or concentration. Measure: clear-zone diameter or area. Keep bacterial strain, agar, disc size, substance volume, time and temperature equal. A larger zone shows greater inhibition under these conditions. Different diffusion rates mean this does not prove effectiveness in a patient. Zone area: Radius = diameter ÷ 2 Area = πr² Diameter 12 mm: radius 6 mm. π × 6² = 113 mm² (3 significant figures). Use squared units. Subtract disc area only if asked. A clear zone means growth was inhibited. Repeated doubling: n = total time ÷ division time Final population = start × 2ⁿ 50 bacteria, 20-minute divisions, 2 hours: 120 ÷ 20 = 6 doublings. 50 × 2⁶ = 3,200 = 3.2 × 10³. Keep time units consistent. Apply the stated growth conditions.

g.title: Bacterial DNA is copied before the cell divides into two; no nucleus or mitotic chromosomes are shown.
